I grepped Mathlib's MvPowerSeries directory for an existing simp lemma about `map` of a polynomial coercion and found none. `coeToMvPowerSeries.ringHom_apply` is already simp in Mathlib. The existing simp attributes (`mem_adicallyRestrictedSubring`, `polynomialToRestricted_coe`, `coeff_adicReduction`, `adicReduction_polynomial`) look well oriented and don't compete with each other. findings.excerpt: theorem map_polynomial_coe {S : Type*} [CommRing S] (g : R →+* S)
findings.problem: This is the canonical push-inside rewrite for `MvPowerSeries.map g ↑p`. The right-hand side has a smaller form (the coercion sits outermost, over `MvPolynomial.map`). It is not tagged `@[simp]`, and Mathlib has no equivalent simp lemma (I found none in Mathlib/RingTheory/MvPowerSeries). Every downstream use therefore has to invoke it by hand. `isAdicallyRestricted_polynomial` (line ~104) feeds it into `simpa only [...]` with `.symm`, and `adicReduction_polynomial` (line 175) uses `rw [..., map_polynomial_coe]`. The coefficient proofs also have to unfold with explicit `coeff_map`/`coeff_coe` lists.
findings.proposed_change: Mark it `@[simp]`. The orientation already pushes `map` through the coercion, and the rewrite terminates because the head `map` disappears. With it, `isAdicallyRestricted_polynomial` and `adicReduction_polynomial` can be closed with a `simp`-based step instead of the explicit `rw`/`.symm` plumbing. The statement can also be written in the `((MvPolynomial.map g p : MvPolynomial σ S) : MvPowerSeries σ S)` form so the coercion elaborates unambiguously.
findings.benefit: Terms such as `map (Ideal.Quotient.mk (I ^ k)) ↑p` normalise to polynomial form automatically. This cuts the manual rewriting in this file and in the many IdealAdicRestricted/* files that work with reductions of polynomials.

findings.problem: This lemma rewrites the coercion of `adicReduction I k f` into the canonical `map (Ideal.Quotient.mk (I ^ k)) ↑f`. Neighbouring lemmas `coeff_adicReduction` and `adicReduction_polynomial` are `@[simp]`, but this one is not. Simp can therefore evaluate coefficients and polynomial reductions, but it cannot unfold the power-series coercion of a reduction. Two proofs have to cite it explicitly: `coeff_adicReduction` does `congrArg ... (adicReduction_coe I k f)` and `adicReduction_polynomial` does `rw [adicReduction_coe, ...]`.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp]` to `adicReduction_coe`. It only fires on the specific `((adicReduction I k f : MvPolynomial ..) : MvPowerSeries ..)` shape. The right-hand side contains no `adicReduction`, so it cannot loop. After adding it, the `rw` in `adicReduction_polynomial` can become part of a `simp` call. Since `coeff_adicReduction` is already simp, check whether the new lemma shadows it: `coeff` of a coercion is rewritten by `MvPolynomial.coeff_coe` first, so the two should agree. Alternatively, keep it non-simp and document that `coeff_adicReduction` is the intended simp entry point.
findings.benefit: This would give a single normal form for reductions viewed as power series (the `map` of the underlying series). Downstream algebra involving `adicReduction` can then be reasoned about with `simp`, using the existing `map_mul`/`map_add` lemmas, instead of citing `adicReduction_coe` by hand.
